content.comment_body: Hi, I have several [version_no] controllers and three [product_name] devices linked to an HMI. For one [product_name] device, I keep getting an alarm: connection is established for a few seconds, then it disconnects, and this loop continues. However, when I access the screen with the buttons for that [product_name] (and the other two), the alarms stop. Does anyone know how to resolve this?
Hello, Could you provide details about the HMI? Which model are you using? Also, how many [version_no] and [product_name] devices are connected to it?

It's a [company_name] TP2200 HMI. I recently added a fourth [product_name] that has the same issue. The HMI is now connected to: 5x [version_no] controllers and 4x [product_name] devices. The alarm message is attached.
Could you upload your [document] for the TIA project and the [product_name] project files (or program code)?
Hello, Note that a TP2200 Comfort panel supports only 8 connections. Please refer to the online help or performance specifications for Comfort panels.
One solution could be sharing display data via master/master connections between the [product_name] controllers, if there is room for data exchange.
Thanks everyone for responding. Could you clarify what you mean by master/master usage?
I can only upload the [product_name] file. The [version_no] project is too large for upload.

[product_name] devices can communicate either using master/slave or master/master modes. In master/slave mode, the slave unit provides its I/Os to the master and runs no program, requiring the slave to be set accordingly. In master/master mode, each device runs its own program and exchanges data. In your project, the units called "LV7 Shop" and "laagspanningsruimte" are using master/master communication. Could you share a screenshot from the TIA project showing which devices the HMI is connected to?

So for example, should I configure all the inputs and outputs of "Douches boven" with network outputs and inputs to another [product_name] device? These devices control valve magnets for showers, enabling night flushes.
Your screenshot shows a "Bovengebied Sauna" [product_name] at IP address 192.168.3.160 which isn't present in your uploaded [product_name] project.
It is included. The initial issue was with "LV7" and the other device was added yesterday. I suspect it's because the system has reached its maximum connections?
In the project you uploaded, there isn't any [product_name] configured for IP address 192.168.3.160.

Your connection screenshot will reveal creation of more than 8 connections. The HMI can't handle more than 8 simultaneous connections. To display data from [product_name] devices not connected to the HMI, first transfer this data to a [product_name] unit that does have an HMI connection. That's what the previous contributor was referring to.
No problem, I uploaded the wrong file earlier. I will try to consolidate everything through one or two [product_name] devices. Thank you!

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants describe recurring connection problems between several [product_name] controllers and a [company_name] HMI panel, where connections cycle between established and disconnected states. The connectivity issue becomes apparent as more devices are added, indicating possible configuration or scalability constraints. Notification messages cease when a relevant HMI screen is open, which points to possible user interface interaction effects or connection management mechanisms.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for reliable communication between the HMI and all [product_name] controllers, wanting connection alarms to stop regardless of which HMI screen is viewed. The user also seeks guidance on network configuration limits and optimal practices for integrating multiple controllers.
